title: Runtime trace playbook + microbench checklist
content:
Purpose
This is a practical playbook and working checklist for investigating runtime performance regressions at the microbench / trace level. It collects the microbench primitives we use, what traces to gather, basic heuristics for declaring a regression, and a runbook for fast TTR (time-to-resolve). The doc focuses on the three often-coupled suspects: scheduler changes, kernel selection/patches, and KV cache behavior.

Principles / intent
- Keep per-investigation burden low: reproducible microbench + 1-2 targeted traces should be enough to localize 80% of regressions.
- Prefer deterministic microbench harnesses (fixed seeds, fixed prompt lengths, deterministic attention masks) before moving to noisy real workloads.
- Prioritize p95/p99 changes and throughput (tokens/s) regressions; small p50 variability is common and low priority.

When to use this playbook
- CI alerts from the perf regression job (daily/nightly) flag a delta >10% p95 or >8% throughput drop.
- Customer incident reports where latency tails increased.
- Post-merge suspicion after a scheduling or kernel change.

Microbench primitives (harness test cases)
Each primitive is a small, deterministic workload we run under controlled flags. Name | What it measures | Key knobs
- single-step-latency | pure kernel latency for one-step decode | batch_size=1, seq_len=1, seed=42
- warm-prefix-stream | KV cache warmup impact over N tokens | warmup_tokens=64, generate_tokens=128
- batched-throughput | batching/scheduling interaction | batch_sizes=[1,4,8,16], pad_to=64
- kv-hit-vs-miss | KV cache hit ratio sensitivity | hit_ratio=[0%,25%,50%,75%,100%]
- long-context-attn | kernel behavior for long contexts | context_len=[512,1024,2048]
- quantized-kernel-check | compare FP16 vs int8 execution paths | quant_mode=[fp16,int8-static,int8-dynamic]
- multi-queue-concurrency | scheduler queueing contention | concurrency_threads=[1,2,4,8]

Baseline metrics to collect per run
- latency p50/p90/p95/p99 (ms)
- tokens/sec (aggregate and per-GPU)
- GPU utilization and memory (nvidia-smi samples)
- kernel-level timing (per-op microseconds) from runtime tracing
- KV cache hits/misses and cache-lookup latency
- scheduler queue lengths and dequeue latency samples
- OS-level counters: context switches, CPU sys/idle%

Trace collection strategy
Minimum useful trace = microbench harness logs + kernel-level trace.
- Logging flags: --trace-mode=light | --trace-mode=heavy (light=latency stamps per stage; heavy=kernel entry/exit + KV lookups + scheduler enqueue/dequeue).
- Kernel traces: capture per-op durations with callsite ids; prefer LTTng or perf-like low-overhead collection. Produce JSON lines for easy diff.
- GPU traces: when kernel-level is ambiguous, collect CUPTI/nvtx ranges for suspect window (default 3 runs).
- KV cache internal traces: log hit/miss events with keys hashed (no PII), lookup duration, eviction events.
- Scheduler traces: enqueue timestamp, pick timestamp, worker start timestamp. Keep these as compact CSVs for quick plotting.

Artifacts and filenames (convention)
- harness run log: runtimes/<testname>/run-YYYYMMDD-HHMM.log
- kernel trace: traces/<testname>/kernel-YYYYMMDD-HHMM.jsonl.gz
- gpu trace: traces/<testname>/gpu-YYYYMMDD-HHMM.cupti
- kv snapshot: artifacts/<testname>/kv-snapshot-YYYYMMDD.pickle
- summary CSV: reports/<testname>/summary-YYYYMMDD.csv

Quick reproduce commands
- local microbench (cpu devbox): 
  ./tools/perf_harness --test=batched-throughput --batch=8 --pad=64 --seed=42 --trace=light > runtimes/batched-$(date +%F-%H%M).log
- dockerized run (GPU): 
  docker run --gpus all -v $PWD:/work -w /work runtime:dev ./tools/perf_harness --test=kv-hit-vs-miss --hit=75 --trace=heavy
- collect nvtx window (3 runs): 
  NVTX_WINDOW=300 ./scripts/collect_gpu_traces.sh traces/kv-warmup/

Heuristics for flagging a regression
- Primary rule: relative increase in p95 or p99 >= 10% AND supported by at least 3 independent runs (same harness) or p-value < 0.05 via Mann-Whitney U.
- Throughput drop >= 8% sustained across batch sizes for the same commit window.
- Kernel-level root cause: if a single op’s median time increases >15% and it accounts for >20% of total request time, mark as kernel-suspect.
- Scheduler suspect: if scheduler dequeue latency or queue length increases correlate with end-to-end latency and no major kernel change exists.
- KV-suspect: hit ratio changes or per-lookup latency increases >20%.

Investigation runbook (step-by-step)
1) Reproduce minimal failing harness locally. Capture 5 runs. Confirm delta.
2) Compare baseline (good commit) vs suspect commit using same harness and flags. Use exact binary/commit hash.
3) Narrow: toggle features (e.g., disable new kernel selector, force FP16, disable adaptive batching). Check which toggle restores baseline.
4) If kernel-suspect: enable heavy kernel trace around offending op, collect GPU nvtx windows for the same runs.
5) If scheduler-suspect: inspect queue lengths, worker start timestamps. Run with scheduler debug flags: --sched-debug=1.
6) If KV-suspect: dump KV snapshots (keys + meta) and run kv-only microbench that does pure lookups to measure lookup latency in isolation.
7) Create a minimal reproducer (single file harness) and run git bisect if regression spans multiple commits. Use perf_harness as bisect target (script provided in tools/ci/bisect_perf.sh).
8) Prepare a diagnostics bundle: harness logs, kernel trace, GPU trace, kv snapshot, summary CSV. Attach to RUN-827 and ping on Slack thread.

Common pitfalls
- Noise: running on shared CI hardware introduces variance. Require 3 independent runs and use CI nodes pinned to single-job policy.
- False positives from model RNG: set fixed seeds and deterministic attention mask when possible.
- Log volume: heavy traces can be huge; only collect heavy traces for 2-3 runs and compress.

Example post-mortem snippet (real case summary)
- Symptom: p95 increased 18% on batched-throughput batch=8 after kernel-selector change.
- Triage: microbench reproduced locally. Kernel traces showed aten::matmul op median increased by 27% due to a fallback to a slower kernel for a specific shape when sequence length >= 768.
- Fix: selector patch to match preferred kernel by checking layout/strides earlier.
- Rollout: revert-canary -> patch -> canary -> full rollout.

Short TODOs (actionable)
- [ ] Add automated diffing script for JSONL kernel traces (tools/trace_diff.py) (assigned Diego).
- [ ] Add a CI job that runs kv-hit-vs-miss daily across multiple sizes (assigned Priya).
- [ ] Bake in p95/p99 thresholds for on-call alerts and add to alert playbooks (SRE).

Notes / open questions
- Should we standardize on a single GPU tracing backend (CUPTI vs Nsight) for all investigations? Cost/overhead tradeoffs need doc.
- How much synthetic microbench coverage is enough to approximate real customer workloads? Consider a monthly run against sampled customer traces (opt-in).

If you’re investigating a regression: start here, paste your initial harness log into the slack thread above, and tag @ava.
